name: Hedgey Finance ClaimCampaigns unvalidated locker approval (Ethereum)
summary: ClaimCampaigns.createLockedCampaign did not validate the claimLockup.tokenLocker address, so a campaign created with an attacker-controlled locker left ClaimCampaigns holding a token allowance to that locker that survived cancelCampaign, letting the attacker spend the protocol's full token balance afterwards.
notes: Top-level deployment of the direct, non-proxy ClaimCampaigns runtime. EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero and the runtime hash is byte-identical at the deployment block and immediately before the exploit.

Loss is the main attacker campaign (0xded2b1a4 driving attack contract 0xc793113f) on Ethereum, measured as exact victim depletion of the ClaimCampaigns contract 0xbc452fdc. USDC: the contract's USDC balance went from 1,303,910.12 (1,303,910,120,000 base units) to 0; the drain transaction 0x2606d459 moved exactly that amount from ClaimCampaigns to the attacker EOA. In the anchor transaction the attacker's own 1,305,000 USDC flash-supplied to fund the campaign flows in and back out (net zero) and is an attacker-supplied input, not victim loss. NOBL (0x88b9f5c6): the attacker received exactly 48,019,408 NOBL from ClaimCampaigns (victim->attacker gross, with 0 NOBL sent back), then dumped it through DEX routers. NOBL is illiquid and was not spot-marked: valuation uses realised proceeds. The attacker's entire Ethereum haul was consolidated into a single 1,987,902.6082287668 DAI transfer to cash-out wallet 0xd84f48b7 in transaction 0x1c2fe7c2 (nonce 103). That net take decomposes as the 1,303,910.12 USDC (valued 1:1) plus 683,992.4882287668 DAI of NOBL sale proceeds (gross DAI received across the campaign was 2,038,902.61, of which ~51,000 DAI was the attacker's own spend acquiring ~684,313 seed NOBL, an excluded attacker input). This ~$1.99M matches Halborn's reported ~$2.1M Ethereum split. The same public vulnerability was independently exploited in separate transactions by other actors (0xf0cad3 drained 120,800 MASA, 0x462412 drained 22,393.28 BLOCK, 0xc0ffeebabe drained 72,688.46 ARC, 0xd1aff3 drained 1,957,142.85773 CO), each after the main campaign; those are distinct campaigns by distinct senders and are not counted here. Later recoveries/returns are not netted.

Scoped to the main attacker campaign on Ethereum. The same public ClaimCampaigns defect was independently exploited by several other actors on Ethereum (draining MASA, BLOCK, ARC and CO in separate transactions) and on Arbitrum (BONUS); those are distinct campaigns and are not counted here.

The Arbitrum leg is intentionally not recorded as a separate incident: its only material victim asset was BONUS, an illiquid token the attacker could not sell (still holding ~76.8M of the ~77.9M drained), so no evidenced USD value or lower bound of at least 1,000 is available and the reported ~$42.6M is an unrealisable spot-mark.
